context:
Batch D investigation 2026-09-26: only 4 retained green DuckDB TPC-H SF1 throughput observations exist (2026-08-11/12/22, values 154k-349k, wide spread, 5+ weeks stale, local runs not nightly). No nightly has retained throughput_at_size yet. Per the item's own data-first rule, setting THROUGHPUT_FLOOR_MEDIAN now would manufacture false failures. Blocked on nightly baseline accumulation.

2026-10-04 adversarial review: the premise changed. Nightly values are retained as check-run annotations (10 values 09-25 to 10-04, 73.6k-98.1k, in two runner-hardware groups), so a baseline exists but a single fixed median would let a fast-runner run drop ~37% unnoticed. Also, the fixed THROUGHPUT_FLOOR_MEDIAN variable contradicts the documented rolling-median model. Moved from blocked to open, with a dependency on throughput-floor-baseline-retention-per-runner (artifact retention and per-runner-class rolling median); activate the floor after that lands.

2026-10-08 status: shipped together with postgres-throughput-uat-cell-unquarantine in draft PR #2757 (head 58142e68f). Finish both after #2757 merges, which waits on the 10-09 and 10-10 green CedarDB nightlies. Do not take or finish before then.
description: Set the numeric Throughput@Size floor: configure THROUGHPUT_FLOOR_MEDIAN and sign off THROUGHPUT_FLOOR_MAX_DROP_FRACTION (default 20%) from the retained rolling-median spread of green DuckDB TPC-H SF1 runs. Wiring, observe-only default, and policy docs merged in #2302 (plus hardening in #2309).
